reconcile.note: Matthew Henry reads Edom's destruction as judgment for its own persistent hostility, not a reversal of Deuteronomy's command to treat Edom as a brother.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen traces the Jacob-Esau brother legend to the historical hatred between Israel and a subjugated Edom.

quotes.text: Edom was a people and a kingdom before Israel, but was then overshadowed by Israel, and even subjugated at last by David: hence the fierce hatred between the brother nations, of which Amos speaks.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 trans.), ch. on the patriarchal legends, on Deuteronomy 23:7 and Edom's fate.

sides.snippet: You shall not abhor an Edomite; for he is your brother: you shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
sides.verseText: You shall not abhor an Edomite; for he is your brother: you shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.

sides.snippet: therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, I will stretch out my hand on Edom, and will cut off man and animal from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman
sides.verseText: therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, I will stretch out my hand on Edom, and will cut off man and animal from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman; even to Dedan shall they fall by the sword.
